gaps: All version tables partial. Most metric fields remainnull because USfactory sources useimperial units/nominal engine litres.

Production versusmodel-year chronology requires further originalbrochure audit; late Aurora/Alero/Intrigue introductions use conventionalMY sequence asboundedidentity chronology.
Early model numbers are grouped wherebody/modelvariant boundaries remainunclear; no duplicate CurvedDashB/F standalonecards.

98 calendar production1940–1942/1946–1996 verified from source; production-checks.json separates true Production labels from model years. Alero starts1998, AuroraI1994/II1999, Bravada1990/1995/2001, Silhouette1989/1996, Toronado1965/1970/1978/1985.
51familycards still not a complete global catalogue. Four generations have selected versions; remaining records have no technical table. No claims of complete facelift or engine coverage.
Jetfire independently named turboF85 branch added with GMHeritage evidence; HurstOlds and several otherspecial packages still need identity audit instead of automatic independentcards.

Photo search bounded/not exhausted:54candidates inspected. Most rejected for model-toys, tightframing, croppedseats/wheels, barriers, openhoods or uncertaingeneration. Suitable Alero candidate8 lacks actualauthor metadata, so credit not invented and photo keptnull.

Most newer Alero/AuroraII/BravadaII–III/Silhouette stock photographs found had only1–3%margin. Keptnull under the requested approximately5%rule; they need a dedicated wider-framed search. CurvedDash museum candidates have chains crossingwheels or tightseatcrops; omitted.
